theory.intro: The **quotient identities** are $\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and $\cot\theta=\dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$. On the unit circle $x=\cos\theta$ and $y=\sin\theta$, so writing everything as sine and cosine simplifies mixed expressions.
facts: $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ needs $\cos\theta \neq 0$, so exclude $\theta = 90^{\circ} + 180^{\circ}k$ in degrees, or $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + k\pi$ in radians, for integer $k$.
$\cot\theta = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$ needs $\sin\theta \neq 0$, so exclude $\theta = 180^{\circ}k$ in degrees, or $\theta = k\pi$ in radians, for integer $k$.

When both $\sin	heta
eq0$ and $\cos	heta
eq0$, $\cot	heta = \dfrac{1}{	an	heta} = \dfrac{1}{\sin	heta/\cos	heta} = \dfrac{\cos	heta}{\sin	heta}$. The quotient $\cot	heta=\dfrac{\cos	heta}{\sin	heta}$ also holds when $\cos	heta=0$, provided $\sin	heta
eq0$.
Multiplying cancels a factor: $\tan\theta \cos\theta = \sin\theta$ when $\cos\theta \neq 0$, and $\cot\theta \sin\theta = \cos\theta$ when $\sin\theta \neq 0$.
Converting every function to sine and cosine is the reliable first move when simplifying a mixed expression.
steps: Rewrite tan as sin/cos and cot as cos/sin
Cancel common factors across numerator and denominator
Express the final result in simplest single-ratio form

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Rewrite cotangent and tangent as sine and cosine.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5\cot\theta\tan\theta\\&=5\times\dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\times\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\\&=5\end{aligned}$

(b) Divide by multiplying by the reciprocal.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{2\tan\theta}{\sin\theta}\\&=\dfrac{2\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\times\dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}\\&=\dfrac{2}{\cos\theta}\\&=2\sec\theta\end{aligned}$

Both expressions require $\sin\theta\ne0$ and $\cos\theta\ne0$.

(a) Write the squared quotient as the square of a ratio.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{6\sin^2\alpha}{\cos^2\alpha}\\&=6\left(\dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha}\right)^2\\&=6\tan^2\alpha\end{aligned}$
This requires $\cos\alpha\ne0$.

(b)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{5\cos^2\alpha}{\sin^2\alpha}\\&=5\left(\dfrac{\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}\right)^2\\&=5\cot^2\alpha\end{aligned}$
This requires $\sin\alpha\ne0$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Simplify for permissible angles:
(a) $2\tan x\operatorname{cosec}x$
(b) $\dfrac{7\tan x}{3\sec x}$
(c) $\dfrac{2\cot x}{\sec x}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Convert both functions to sine and cosine.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2\tan x\operatorname{cosec}x\\&=2\times\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\times\dfrac{1}{\sin x}\\&=\dfrac{2}{\cos x}\\&=2\sec x\end{aligned}$
This requires $\sin x\ne0$ and $\cos x\ne0$.

(b) Dividing by secant means multiplying by cosine.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{7\tan x}{3\sec x}\\&=\dfrac{7\sin x}{\cos x}\times\dfrac{\cos x}{3}\\&=\dfrac{7}{3}\sin x\end{aligned}$
This requires $\cos x\ne0$.

(c) The cosine factors multiply.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{2\cot x}{\sec x}\\&=\dfrac{2\cos x}{\sin x}\times\cos x\\&=\dfrac{2\cos^2x}{\sin x}\end{aligned}$
This requires $\sin x\ne0$ and $\cos x\ne0$.

(a) Keep the coefficient outside the power.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{5\sin^4\beta}{4\cos^4\beta}\\&=\dfrac{5}{4}\left(\dfrac{\sin\beta}{\cos\beta}\right)^4\\&=\dfrac{5}{4}\tan^4\beta\end{aligned}$
This requires $\cos\beta\ne0$.

(b)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\dfrac{3\cos^6\beta}{7\sin^6\beta}\\&=\dfrac{3}{7}\left(\dfrac{\cos\beta}{\sin\beta}\right)^6\\&=\dfrac{3}{7}\cot^6\beta\end{aligned}$
This requires $\sin\beta\ne0$.

workedExamples.question_text: Prove that $5\sin x\cot x\sec x=5$ for permissible angles $x$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Start with the left-hand side and rewrite cotangent and secant.
$\begin{aligned}\text{LHS}&=5\sin x\cot x\sec x\\&=5\sin x\times\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\times\dfrac{1}{\cos x}\\&=5\\&=\text{RHS}\end{aligned}$
The original expression requires $\sin x\ne0$ and $\cos x\ne0$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Prove for permissible angles:
(a) $\dfrac{3+\cot\theta}{1+3\tan\theta}=\cot\theta$
(b) $\dfrac{2\operatorname{cosec}x+\sec x}{2+\tan x}=\operatorname{cosec}x$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Rewrite in sine and cosine, then combine each numerator and denominator.
$\begin{aligned}\text{LHS}&=\dfrac{3+\cos\theta/\sin\theta}{1+3\sin\theta/\cos\theta}\\&=\dfrac{(3\sin\theta+\cos\theta)/\sin\theta}{(\cos\theta+3\sin\theta)/\cos\theta}\\&=\dfrac{3\sin\theta+\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\times\dfrac{\cos\theta}{\cos\theta+3\sin\theta}\\&=\dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\\&=\cot\theta\\&=\text{RHS}\end{aligned}$
This requires $\sin\theta\ne0$, $\cos\theta\ne0$ and $\cos\theta+3\sin\theta\ne0$.

(b)
$\begin{aligned}\text{LHS}&=\dfrac{2/\sin x+1/\cos x}{2+\sin x/\cos x}\\&=\dfrac{(2\cos x+\sin x)/(\sin x\cos x)}{(2\cos x+\sin x)/\cos x}\\&=\dfrac{2\cos x+\sin x}{\sin x\cos x}\times\dfrac{\cos x}{2\cos x+\sin x}\\&=\dfrac{1}{\sin x}\\&=\operatorname{cosec}x\\&=\text{RHS}\end{aligned}$
This requires $\sin x\ne0$, $\cos x\ne0$ and $2\cos x+\sin x\ne0$.

foundation.solution_text:
$\cot x \sec x = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} \times \dfrac{1}{\cos x}$
$=\dfrac{1}{\sin x}$
$=\operatorname{cosec} x$

development.question_text: Simplify $\dfrac{5\tan A}{2\sec A}$ for permissible angles $A$.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{5\tan A}{2\sec A}=\dfrac{5\sin A/\cos A}{2/\cos A}$
$=\dfrac{5\sin A}{\cos A}\times\dfrac{\cos A}{2}$
$=\dfrac{5}{2}\sin A$

development.question_text: Simplify $\dfrac{\tan A}{\sin A}$ for permissible angles $A$.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\tan A}{\sin A} = \dfrac{\sin A/\cos A}{\sin A}$
$=\dfrac{1}{\cos A}$
$=\sec A$

development.question_text: Simplify $\dfrac{\cot B}{\cos B}$ for permissible angles $B$.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\cot B}{\cos B} = \dfrac{\cos B/\sin B}{\cos B}$
$=\dfrac{1}{\sin B}$
$=\operatorname{cosec} B$

mastery.question_text: Prove that $\dfrac{3\operatorname{cosec}x+\sec x}{3+\tan x}=\operatorname{cosec}x$ for permissible angles $x$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{LHS}=\dfrac{3/\sin x+1/\cos x}{3+\sin x/\cos x}$
$=\dfrac{(3\cos x+\sin x)/(\sin x\cos x)}{(3\cos x+\sin x)/\cos x}$
$=\dfrac{3\cos x+\sin x}{\sin x\cos x}\times\dfrac{\cos x}{3\cos x+\sin x}$
$=\dfrac{1}{\sin x}$
$=\operatorname{cosec}x$
$=\text{RHS}$
